the symbiont is transmitted from adult females to their offspring by the symbiont encapsulation system in M. punctatissima.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the female-specific system for the symbionts in plataspid stinbugs is a unique example of the "maternal effect" in insects, and that the system is an excellent model system for investigating the mechanisms of the symbionts and the host insects.
the plataspid symbiosis is an example of "symbiosis with a cost", in which the host incurs a substantial reproductive cost for the symbiotic transmission.

the plataspid insect has developed a unique, complex system for vertical transmission of symbionts, and that this is a good model system for the study of the evolutionary process of symbiont transmission in insects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the symbiont is a very costly burden for the insect host, which is why the host has evolved such a sophisticated system for symbionts to be transmitted from mother to offspring.
the plataspid symbiont transmission system is a complex and highly specialized system, and it has been evolved to ensure the efficient vertical transmission of the beneficial bacterial symbionts.
the symbiont is not just a passenger in the insect body, but rather it is an important partner that is actively maintained by the host.
